Heman the Singer
HEE-man
proper noun
From the Hebrew Heman, “faithful” or “trusty,” a Levitical singer and the king’s seer, set over the song in the house of the LORD.

📖 Biblical Definition

Heman was a Levite of the sons of Kohath, a singer appointed by David and the king’s seer, set with Asaph and Jeduthun over the song in the house of the LORD. When the ministers of music were ordained, the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, were appointed to sound with cymbals of brass (1Ch 15:17, 19), and David and the captains of the host separated to the service the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals (1Ch 25:1). Heman is called the king’s seer in the words of God, and God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters; all these were under the hands of their father for song in the house of the LORD (1Ch 25:5-6). His name stands also in the title of the eighty-eighth Psalm, A Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite, the darkest of the songs, a prayer out of the depths of affliction. The dictionary marks Heman as a chief of the temple-singers and a seer, whose office joined music and prophecy in the worship of God; for the song of the sanctuary was no mere ornament but a prophetic ministry, that the saints might sing with grace in their hearts to the Lord (Col 3:16). His house, set apart for praise, teaches that worship is a holy and ordered service, appointed of God and committed to His servants, and that even the song of deepest grief, as in his psalm, is offered up unto the LORD who heareth the cry of the afflicted.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A Levitical singer and the king’s seer, set over the song in the house of the LORD.

HEMAN THE SINGER, a Levite set over the song in the house of the LORD.

He was appointed with Asaph and Jeduthun to the temple music.

He sounded with cymbals of brass when the ark was brought up.

He is called the king’s seer in the words of God.

His name stands in the title of the eighty-eighth Psalm.

📖 Key Scripture

1Ch 6:33 — "And these are they that waited with their children. Of the sons of the Kohathites: Heman a singer, the son of Joel, the son of Shemuel,"

1Ch 25:1 — "Moreover David and the captains of the host separated to the service of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals: and the number of the workmen according to their service was:"

1Ch 25:5 — "All these were the sons of Heman the king's seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. And God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters."

Col 3:16 — "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A figure of Scripture; Heman witnesses to the ordered, prophetic ministry of song in the worship of God.

expand to see more

Heman has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as a chief of the temple-singers and the king’s seer. The dictionary records him that the reader may mark the holy office of song appointed in the house of the LORD.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that worship is a holy and ordered service, appointed of God and committed to His servants, and that the song of the sanctuary is a prophetic ministry, not a mere ornament. Heman was set over the song with Asaph and Jeduthun, and is called the king’s seer; his sons prophesied with harps and psalteries and cymbals. So the dictionary honours the place of godly music in worship, that the word of Christ dwell richly in the saints, who sing with grace in their hearts to the Lord. And the eighty-eighth Psalm, the darkest of all, bearing his name, teaches that even the song of deepest affliction is offered up to the LORD who heareth the cry of His own.
